(Natchitoches, Louisiana) | college = * [[LSU Tigers men's basketball|LSU]] (2017–2018) * [[Pearl River Community College|Pearl River CC]] (2018–2019) * [[Tulsa Golden Hurricane men's basketball|Tulsa]] (2019–2021) | draft_year = 2021 | career_start = 2021 | years1 = [[2021–22 NBA G League season|2021]]–[[2022–23 NBA G League season|2023]] | team1 = [[Long Island Nets]] | years2 = [[2023–24 NBA G League season|2024]] | team2 = [[Austin Spurs]] | highlights = * Second-team All-[[American Athletic Conference|AAC]] (2021) * Third-team All-AAC (2020) }} '''Brandon Tyree Rachal''' (born September 30, 1999) is an American professional [[basketball]] player who last played for the [[Austin Spurs]] of the [[NBA G League]]. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[LSU Tigers men's basketball|LSU Tigers]], the [[Pearl River Community College|Pearl River CC Wildcats]], and the [[Tulsa Golden Hurricane men's basketball|Tulsa Golden Hurricane]]. ==High school career== Rachal played basketball for [[Natchitoches Central High School]] in his hometown of [[Natchitoches, Louisiana]]. He helped his team win two state titles with one runner-up finish. In his junior season, Rachal averaged 15 points, eight rebounds and three steals per game. He led his team to a Class 5A state championship and was named MVP of the title game.{{cite web |last1=Lopez |first1=Andrew |title=LSU basketball picks up commitment from Natchitoches Central guard Brandon Rachal |url=https://www.nola.com/sports/high_schools/article_f5eb0164-5c15-5061-8e9d-e0e57e81ccc7.html |website=[[The Times-Picayune/The New Orleans Advocate|The Times-Picayune]] |access-date=August 1, 2021 |date=October 12, 2016}} As a senior, he averaged 20 points, 12 rebounds and three steals per game.{{cite web |last1=Lopez |first1=Andrew |title=Meet LSU's 2017 basketball signing class |url=https://www.nola.com/sports/article_7692cbeb-b395-5a94-9c08-fa4ef7092837.html |website=[[The Times-Picayune/The New Orleans Advocate|The Times-Picayune]] |access-date=August 1, 2021 |date=April 20, 2017}} A four-star recruit, Rachal committed to playing college basketball for [[LSU Tigers men's basketball|LSU]] over offers from [[Texas Longhorns men's basketball|Texas]] and [[Texas A&M Aggies men's basketball|Texas A&M]], among others.{{cite web |last1=Daniel |first1=Cody |title=4-star CG Brandon Rachal commits to LSU over Texas, Texas A&M |url=https://www.burntorangenation.com/2016/10/12/13252292/brandon-rachal-texas-longhorns-lsu-tigers-texas-a-m-aggies-commitment |website=Burnt Orange Nation |access-date=August 1, 2021 |date=October 12, 2016}} He reaffirmed his commitment to LSU after head coach [[Johnny Jones (basketball, born 1961)|Johnny Jones]] was replaced by [[Will Wade]].{{cite web |last1=Mickles |first1=Sheldon |title=All's well that ends well: LSU basketball signee Brandon Rachal still set to join Tigers program, coach says |url=https://www.theadvocate.com/baton_rouge/sports/lsu/article_4913fafc-100d-11e7-8394-3f7fcdc4866e.html |website=[[The Advocate (Louisiana)|The Advocate]] |access-date=August 1, 2021 |date=March 23, 2017}} Rachal also played [[American football|football]] at the [[wide receiver]] position in high school and was recruited by [[college football]] programs.{{cite web |last1=Roser |first1=Jerit |title=LSU, Tulane hoops 2017 target Brandon Rachal gaining football recruiting momentum |url=https://www.nola.com/sports/high_schools/article_75cf2a3d-7e11-5b67-a442-6e7bf73e6e1d.html |website=[[The Times-Picayune/The New Orleans Advocate|The Times-Picayune]] |access-date=August 1, 2021 |date=January 14, 2016}} ==College career== On January 29, 2018, Rachal was suspended for one game by LSU for violating team rules.{{cite web |last1=Guilbeau |first1=Glenn |title=LSU players Sims, Rachal were suspended apparently due to appearance in a video |url=https://www.theadvertiser.com/story/sports/college/lsu/2018/01/30/film-study-lsu-basketball-players-wayde-sims-and-brandon-rachal-were-suspended-partly-because-their/1079877001/ |website=[[The Daily Advertiser (Lafayette, Louisiana)|The Daily Advertiser]] |access-date=July 31, 2021 |date=January 30, 2018}} He was suspended for LSU's two games at the [[2018 National Invitation Tournament|National Invitational Tournament]] for undisclosed reasons.{{cite web |last1=Mickles |first1=Sheldon |title=After transfer, former LSU guard Brandon Rachal lands at Pearl River Community College |url=https://www.theadvocate.com/baton_rouge/sports/lsu/article_8d53d712-95b5-11e8-86b4-f34bbaa868a1.html |website=[[The Advocate (Louisiana)|The Advocate]] |access-date=July 31, 2021 |date=August 1, 2018}} As a freshman, Rachal averaged 4.4 points and 3.3 rebounds per game. For his sophomore season, he moved to [[Pearl River Community College]].{{cite web |last1=Lopez |first1=Andrew |title=Former LSU guard Brandon Rachal lands at Pearl River CC |url=https://www.nola.com/archive/article_e68a98da-2be3-59a5-9a05-62887765d908.html |website=[[The Times-Picayune/The New Orleans Advocate|The Times-Picayune]] |access-date=July 31, 2021 |date=August 1, 2018}} Rachal averaged 15.5 points, 8.7 rebounds and 2.7 assists per game, earning Second Team [[National Junior College Athletic Association]] All-American honors.{{cite web |last1=Hines |first1=Kelly |title=TU basketball lands junior college standout Brandon Rachal |url=https://tulsaworld.com/sports/college/tu/tu-basketball-lands-junior-college-standout-brandon-rachal/article_a23933d4-7946-55b6-9ba4-04e6197925fa.html |website=[[Tulsa World]] |access-date=August 1, 2021 |date=April 9, 2019}} For his junior season, he transferred to [[Tulsa Golden Hurricane men's basketball|Tulsa]]. On November 16, 2019, he recorded a career-high 30 points, seven rebounds and five steals in a 72–65 victory against [[Austin Peay Governors basketball|Austin Peay]].{{cite web |title=TU men's basketball: Rachal scores 30 points as Hurricane tops Austin Peay |url=https://tulsaworld.com/sports/college/tu/tu-mens-basketball-rachal-scores-30-points-as-hurricane-tops-austin-peay/article_0e8ce09c-4266-545f-b02a-5a09d09903cd.html |website=[[Tulsa World]] |access-date=August 1, 2021 |date=November 16, 2019}} As a junior, Rachal averaged 12.1 points and 5.8 rebounds per game, and was named to the Third Team All-[[American Athletic Conference]] (AAC).{{cite web |last1=Hines |first1=Kelly |title=TU's Martins Igbanu selected to all-conference first team; Brandon Rachal on third team |url=https://tulsaworld.com/sports/college/tu/tus-martins-igbanu-selected-to-all-conference-first-team-brandon-rachal-on-third-team/article_c415f072-f37d-572b-b9f0-9ba88fbe8d7e.html |website=[[Tulsa World]] |access-date=August 1, 2021 |date=March 10, 2020}} On January 2, 2021, he posted a senior season-high 25 points and 13 rebounds in a 70–66 win over [[Cincinnati Bearcats men's basketball|Cincinnati]].{{cite web |title=Rachal scores 25 to lead Tulsa past Cincinnati 70-66 |url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/ncaab/2021/01/02/rachal-scores-25-to-lead-tulsa-past-cincinnati-70-66/115246628/ |website=[[USA Today]] |publisher=[[Associated Press]] |access-date=August 1, 2021 |date=January 2, 2021}} Rachal was named Naismith Player of the Week on January 4.{{cite web |title=Rachal Named Naismith Trophy Jersey Mikes Player of the Week |url=https://tulsahurricane.com/news/2021/1/4/mens-basketball-rachal-named-naismith-trophy-jersey-mikes-player-of-the-week.aspx |website=[[Tulsa Golden Hurricane]] |access-date=August 1, 2021 |date=January 4, 2021}} As a senior, he averaged 15 points, 7.2 rebounds and 2.2 assists per game, and was a Second Team All-AAC selection.{{cite web |title=Brandon Rachal – Men's Basketball |url=https://tulsahurricane.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/brandon-rachal/9777 |website=University of Tulsa Athletics |access-date=August 1, 2021}} ==Professional career== ===Long Island Nets (2021–2023)=== After going undrafted in the [[2021 NBA draft]], Rachal joined the [[Brooklyn Nets]] for [[2021 NBA Summer League]].{{cite web|first=Chris|last=Milholen|title=UNDRAFTED: Nets sign David Duke Jr. and Brandon Rachal as Summer League roster fills out|url=https://www.netsdaily.com/2021/7/31/22603511/undrafted-nets-sign-david-duke-jr-and-brandon-rachal-as-summer-league-roster-fills-out|website=NetsDaily.com|publisher=[[SB Nation]]|date=July 31, 2021|access-date=October 13, 2021}} On October 11, 2021, Rachal signed with the Nets.{{cite web|first=Alec|last=Sturm|title=Long Island Nets continue to round out roster, sign Jordan Bowden and Brandon Rachal|url=https://www.netsdaily.com/2021/10/11/22721556/long-island-nets-continue-to-round-out-roster-sign-jordan-bowden-and-brandon-rachal|website=NetsDaily.com|publisher=[[SB Nation]]|date=October 11, 2021|access-date=October 15, 2021}} He was waived at the end of training camp on October 15.{{cite web|first=Zach|last=Braziller|title=Nic Claxton's defensive versatility makes him underrated asset to Nets |url=https://nypost.com/2021/10/16/nic-claxtons-defensive-versatility-an-underrated-nets-asset/|work=New York Post|date=October 16, 2021|access-date=October 17, 2021|quote=On Friday, the Nets waived guards Jordan Bowden and Brandon Rachal. They could end up with their G-League affiliate, the Long Island Nets.}} On October 25, 2021, Rachal joined the [[Long Island Nets]].{{cite web|title=Long Island Nets announce training camp roster|url=https://longisland.gleague.nba.com/news/long-island-nets-announce-training-camp-roster-2|website=NBA.com|date=October 25, 2021|access-date=October 25, 2021}} Rachal again signed with the Brooklyn Nets on October 1, 2022, but was waived on October 5. He rejoined Long Island on October 9. On January 23, 2023, Rachal was waived after appearing in 1 game. He was acquired by the [[Fort Wayne Mad Ants]] from waivers, on February 27.{{Cite web | title=NBA G League Transactions - The NBA G League | url=https://gleague.nba.com/transactions | access-date=2025-02-15 | website=gleague.nba.com}} He was waived on March 8 without appearing in a game. On October 30, 2023, Rachal joined the [[Rip City Remix]] of the [[NBA G League]],{{cite tweet|first=Casey|last=Holdahl|title=The @ripcityremix begin training camp for their {{as written|ina|gural [sic]}} season today at the @trailblazers practice facility. Here's who they're taking into camp...|number=1719017456981696590|user=CHold|date=October 30, 2023|access-date=November 12, 2023}} but was waived on November 7.{{cite web|title=2023-2024 Rip City Remix Transactions History|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/gleague/teams/Rip-City-Remix/67/Transaction-History/2024|website=RealGM.com|access-date=November 12, 2023}} ===Austin Spurs (2024)=== On March 4, 2024, Rachal joined the [[Austin Spurs]].{{cite web|title=2023-2024 Austin Spurs Transaction History|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/gleague/teams/Austin-Spurs/9/Transaction_History/2024|website=RealGM.com|access-date=March 4, 2024}} ==Career statistics== {{NBA player statistics legend}}
